summary.headline: ICICI Bank Q1 FY27: PBT excluding treasury rose 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore; NIM 4.36%, loans up 19.6% YoY.
summary.overview: ICICI Bank posted strong Q1 FY27 profit growth, with PBT excluding treasury up 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore and PAT up 15.9% to ₹14,805 crore. Net interest margin expanded to 4.36% from 4.32% in Q4, helped by about 8 bps from income tax refund interest; excluding that, NIM was 4.28%. Loan growth accelerated to 19.6% YoY, led by a sequential pickup in domestic corporate (up 6.9% QoQ) and business banking, while asset quality was stable with net NPA at 0.35%. Management guided NIM to be range-bound in FY27 but flagged possible dilution from the FCNR(B) mobilisation push, and gave no FCNR amounts raised so far.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.32% in Q4 FY26 and 4.34% in Q1 FY26; 4.28% ex tax-refund interest
0.32% of average advances; 6.2% of core operating profit

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail loans grew 12.0% YoY (2.7% QoQ) and are 41.1% of total portfolio incl. non-fund; mortgages +14.6% YoY, personal loans +12.9% YoY (+4.0% QoQ), credit cards -1.9% YoY, auto loans +3.6% YoY.

segments.name: Rural (incl. gold loans)
segments.commentary: Rural portfolio grew 35.4% YoY and 6.2% QoQ; gold loans form a substantial part but are not disclosed separately.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Business banking loans grew 28.2% YoY and 6.9% QoQ.

segments.name: Domestic corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 18.5% YoY and 6.9% QoQ; NBFC and HFC exposure rose to ₹92,052 crore (4.5% of advances) from ₹85,904 crore in March 2026; builder book ₹74,721 crore (4.3% of loans).

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Overseas loan portfolio was 3.1% of total loan book at June 30, 2026.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to be range-bound in FY27 assuming no rate movements, with possible slight dilution from FCNR(B) programme and loans against FCNR deposits.
FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging estimated at about 6.30-6.40%, versus 6% coupon; no mobilisation amount or leverage levels disclosed; detail promised with Q2 results.
ECL transition from April 1, 2027: no material net worth impact expected, per management; ongoing credit cost impact not quantified.
Management indicated normalised credit cost of about 50 bps excluding chunky recoveries, versus reported 32 bps.
Average loan growth expected to be somewhat lower than the 19.6% period-end figure.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 7,608 after 97 branch openings in Q1 FY27; 12,190 ATMs and cash recycling machines.
Average LCR for the quarter about 124% versus 128% a year ago.
Contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore (about 0.8% of advances) held at June 30, 2026; additional standard asset provision of ₹1,283 crore (made Q3 FY26 on agri priority sector) still held.
Technology expenses about 11.4% of operating expenses.
ICICI Life VNB ₹571 crore with VNB margin 26.7% vs 24.7% in FY26; ICICI General combined ratio 107.2% vs 102.9%.
demand_pricing: Corporate demand rose on working capital needs and a shift away from bond and equity markets; management said there is no corporate loan target and lending depends on risk, return and pricing thresholds.

Fee income growth was broad-based across cards, loan processing, transaction banking, trade, forex and deposit-linked fees, with a base effect from weak Q1 FY26; credit card book is declining on lower revolver rates.
Cost of deposits 4.41% vs 4.43% in Q4 FY26 and 4.85% in Q1 FY26; about 57% of domestic loans linked to repo and external benchmarks, 13% to MCLR, 30% fixed.
Gross NPA additions ₹5,552 crore vs ₹6,245 crore a year ago; corporate NPA formation minimal; retail and rural additions ₹4,331 crore including ₹706 crore from KCC.
Management described competition from PSU banks as present but not holding back growth; said it is not doing business at certain quoted rates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.36% NIM sustainable and what levers exist, and what drove the slippage rise and West Asia stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax refund interest added about 8 bps; FY27 NIM expected range-bound absent rate moves, with FCNR dilution risk. Management said the quarter-on-quarter slippage rise is seasonal (KCC-related); Q1 FY27 gross additions of ₹5,552 crore compared with ₹6,245 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: How much has been mobilised under FCNR(B), at what leverage, and will rates go above 6%?
qa_highlights.answer: No amount or leverage disclosed; management said rates will be calibrated, funding will come from partner banks, bond issuance and unleveraged inflows, and no need to raise rates above 6% currently. Details expected with Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% loan growth sustainable and where is the corporate demand coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth reflects system momentum from policy measures, that there are no segment targets, and that corporate demand reflects working capital needs and bond/equity market moderation. Average loan growth will be somewhat lower than the period-end rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the agri (KCC) provision write-back and the ECL transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Remediation of the agri portfolio is under validation before any provision write-back; no timeline given. ECL from April 2027 expected to have no net worth impact, with Stage 2 provisioning raising ongoing costs partly offset by Stage 3 changes; quantum not estimated.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off recovery in Q1, and what is the normalised credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: One NCLT-driven recovery on an asset previously sold to NARCL came through this quarter. Reported credit cost 32 bps; normalised about 50 bps excluding chunky recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving fee income growth and card/personal loan trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee growth reflects broad business momentum plus a low base; sequential fee increase about ₹500 crore. Personal loans grew 12% YoY and 4% QoQ; cards growth is weak due to lower revolver rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and NRI share of deposits, and surplus SLR?
qa_highlights.answer: LCR about 124% vs 128% a year ago. Surplus SLR and NRI share of deposits not disclosed; management expects NRI share to rise as FCNR(B) flows pick up.

risks_watch: FCNR(B) programme could dilute NIM and raise funding costs via leverage and partner bank tie-ups; mobilisation size undisclosed.
Credit cost seasonality in Q1 and Q3 (agri/KCC); West Asia and energy shock impact on borrowers, with management reporting no specific concern currently.
Corporate and business banking growth sustainability at 18-28% YoY, with management monitoring West Asia and El Nino effects on customer selection.
ECL transition from April 2027, with Stage 2 provisioning raising ongoing provisions; quantum not yet estimated.
Pending agri (KCC) remediation and possible provision write-back timing, not yet guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and asset quality, but evasive on FCNR(B) volumes, leverage levels, and the timing of agri provision write-back and ECL impact. Management repeatedly declined to give numerical targets, citing early days and 'calibrated' approach.
key_quotes: We do not have any targets across any segment, and in particular, corporate loan as well.
It is mathematically impossible for the two to not go hand in hand.
As long as these two things are met, we are happy to lend to that segment.

adds.what: 97 branch openings in Q1 FY27 (branch network at 7,608)

growth.why: Management guides NIM range-bound in FY27 (no rate moves) with slight FCNR(B) dilution and average loan growth somewhat below the 19.6% period-end rate, with no quantified revenue target; Q1 loans +19.6% YoY and PBT ex-treasury +20.9% YoY, backed by demand and branch additions rather than disclosed capacity or orders.
